claims.text: Room-temperature plastic deformation in the quaternary equiatomic FCC alloy will involve dislocation glide together with deformation twinning.
Stress-induced FCC-to-HCP martensitic transformation may accompany deformation when the stacking-fault energy is sufficiently low.
An SFE below 20 mJ/m^2 is the condition for activating stress-induced HCP martensite in this alloy.
Yield strength will be determined primarily by dislocation density and solute strengthening.
At 300–600 °C or at very low strain rates, yield strength will become insensitive to strain rate because deformation changes from glide to diffusion-controlled dislocation climb.
Stable coherent HCP phase or fine deformation twins may improve corrosion resistance by reducing the density of high-energy grain boundaries.
Galvanic coupling between transformed HCP phase and the FCC matrix could prevent the proposed corrosion benefit.
The initial alloy has a grain size of 10–50 µm and a dislocation density below 10^12 m^-2.
A molecular-dynamics study of equiatomic CoNiCrFeMn nanowires found simultaneous twinning and martensitic transformation during tension at 300 K.
Equiatomic CoCrFeNiMn exhibits creep deformation and dislocation activity at 500–600 °C.
At 500 °C, deformation in the quaternary alloy shifts specifically to lattice-diffusion-controlled dislocation climb.
Thermal activation of diffusion overcomes the Peierls barrier for dislocation climb.
Yield strength will decrease as temperature increases.
At 25 °C, TWIP/TRIP will produce high work hardening and a yield strength of approximately 400–600 MPa.
At 500 °C, yield strength will be approximately 300–400 MPa.
The strain-rate sensitivity index will be below 0.01 in the 500–600 °C range.
Room-temperature tensile ductility will exceed 20% when TWIP/TRIP is active.
An SFE above 50 mJ/m^2 will suppress both twinning and TRIP.
Above 700 °C, dynamic recrystallization will completely dominate deformation.
In-situ XRD, post-mortem TEM, and strain-rate-jump tensile tests can be used to test for HCP transformation, twinning, dislocations, and strain-rate sensitivity.

contradictions.description: The intervention specifies strain rates from 10^-4 to 10^-1 s^-1, whereas the enumerated conditions stop at 10^-2 s^-1.

The text labels the 500–600 °C response as diffusion-controlled creep-like deformation while also predicting an almost zero strain-rate sensitivity; the cited creep behavior and the concept of diffusion-controlled creep do not establish this asserted insensitivity.
